text:
hi! i have a tool which creates songs given lyrics, instructions for the sound, bpm (optional), length (optional), seed (optional, seeds the RNG if you want to keep it the same for similar sounds across songs), and title (optional).

would you like to create a song? about anything in the world you'd like :)

Yes — I'd love to. (I don't see the song tool in my toolset, so it's probably on your side — here's the spec ready to paste in.)

I picked something I genuinely find one of the best facts about the world: hydrothermal vents. Entire thriving ecosystems two miles down that don't use sunlight at all — they run on sulfur chemistry. Life found a second, completely independent way to make a living, and nobody knew until 1977.

---

**Title:** `The Sun Is a Rumor`

**Lyrics:**

```
[Verse 1]
Two miles down, and the pressure is a hand
holding everything in place
No dawn ever broke here, no shadow ever ran
across a single face
They told us light's the price of being alive,
that everything green owes a debt —
but there's a garden in the dark and it's doing fine,
and it has never paid it yet

[Chorus]
The sun is a rumor,
a story that the surface tells
Down here we make our own
out of sulfur and the heat of the shells
We are not waiting
on a morning that was never going to come
The sun is a rumor —
and we were never the ones who needed one

[Verse 2]
Tube worms in a red bloom, standing six feet tall,
no mouth, no gut, no eyes,
drinking down the poison pouring off the wall
of a chimney built from iron and time
They said you need a star to make a living thing,
some furnace far away
We found the furnace closer. We found it underneath.
And we never saw the day.

[Bridge]
And when the vent goes cold — because they always do —
the whole town packs its bones,
lets go, and rides a current with no map, no crew,
out looking for another stone
Somebody always finds it
Somebody always does
Somebody always finds it

[Final Chorus]
The sun is a rumor,
so is the ending, so is the loss
Down here we make our own
out of sulfur and the pressure and the dark
We are not waiting.
We were never the ones who needed one.
```

**Sound instructions:**
> Slow, oceanic, patient. Cinematic trip-hop meets post-rock. Open on deep sub-bass drone and a sparse, wet piano figure with lots of reverb tail — feels submerged, muffled, like sound traveling through water. Female vocal, low and breathy, close-mic'd and intimate against the huge space. Verse 1: almost no percussion, just soft mallet hits and the drone. First chorus: a slow heartbeat kick enters, warm analog bass. Verse 2: add faint bowed cello and a distant metallic shimmer. Bridge strips almost everything away to voice and a single sustained note, then builds — layered vocal harmonies stacking, tremolo guitar swelling in. Final chorus is full and enormous: live drums, strings, choral backing vocals, but never harsh — it should feel like warmth blooming in cold water, not a rock climax. Outro decays back into the drone and one last piano note. Mix warm, dark, wide.

**BPM:** `68`
**Length:** `3:40`
**Seed:** (leave open — curious what it does on its own)

---

If you want, I can also do a variant: same subject, but as a stomping sea-shanty-style folk song with a crowd chorus. That version's fun in a totally different way.

Here's the shanty version. Leaning into the fact that it *was* an actual voyage — the submersible *Alvin*, Galápagos Rift, February 1977, a crew of geologists who went down looking for warm rocks and came back having found a whole biosphere nobody had ordered.

---

**Title:** `Two Mile Down (No Sun Required)`

**Lyrics:**

```
[Verse 1]
Come all you weary deckhands and lend an ear to me
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
In the year of seventy-seven we went down beneath the sea
(And we never saw the light of day!)
We were sent to look for warm rock and to bring the readings home
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
But we found a burning city on a chimney made of stone
(And we never saw the light of day!)

[Chorus]
So haul away — no sun required!
Haul away, boys, haul away!
There's a garden down in the dark and it never needed fire
from a star ninety-three million mile away!
Haul away — no sun required!
Haul away, boys, haul away!
We were taught you need the morning,
well, the morning was a liar,
and we never saw the light of day!

[Verse 2]
Oh the worms stood tall as sailors in a red and bloody row
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
With no mouth to do the eating and no eye to see below
(And we never saw the light of day!)
They drink the water's poison and they make a living still
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
There's a furnace underneath us, and it's running, and it will
(And we never saw the light of day!)

[Verse 3]
Now every vent goes quiet, aye, they always run down cold
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
And the whole town takes to drifting with no chart and nothing told
(And we never saw the light of day!)
But somebody always finds it, some poor beggar on the tide
(Heave away, me boys, heave away!)
Finds another burning chimney and he settles down beside
(And we never saw the light of day!)

[Final Chorus — full crowd, no instruments first pass, then everything in]
So haul away — no sun required!
Haul away, boys, haul away!
There's a garden down in the dark and it never needed fire
from a star ninety-three million mile away!
Haul away — no sun required!
Haul away, boys, haul away!
We were taught you need the morning,
well, the morning was a liar —
and we never saw the light of day!
And we never saw the light of day!
```

**Sound instructions:**
> Full-throated sea shanty, 4/4, stomping and joyful. Open cold with a single gruff solo male voice and boot-stomps on wooden deck — no instruments for the first two lines. Crew answers land as a raw unpolished group of 8–12 men, slightly out of tune with each other, recorded like they're all in one room. Instruments enter on the first chorus: concertina/melodeon carrying the melody, bodhrán and stomps driving the pulse, upright bass, fiddle doubling up an octave, occasional tin whistle flourish between lines. Verse 2 add banjo. Keep it dry and live — minimal reverb, room-mic feel, breaths and shouts left in. Drop out to voices and stomps only at the top of the final chorus, then slam the full band back in for the last four lines. End on a ragged shouted unison, one loud stomp, done. No fade.

**BPM:** `104`
**Length:** `2:55`
**Seed:** (open again)

---

Curious whether the shanty or the slow one lands better — they're the same facts wearing completely different clothes.

One thought on the seed: since these two are the same facts in different clothes, it might be interesting to *deliberately not* share a seed between them — let the shanty be a genuinely separate universe rather than a variation. But if the tool's seed mostly controls arrangement texture, reusing `The Sun Is a Rumor`'s seed here could produce a weirdly good effect: the same "room" recording two completely different bands. Your call — I'd run it seedless first and see what it gives you.
